desc:
For an index i of the array nums, split the array into the first i + 1 elements (the head) and the remaining n - i - 1 elements (the tail). The average difference of i is the absolute value of floor(average of head) - floor(average of tail). The average of an empty tail is defined as 0, and an average is the sum divided by the element count, rounded down.

Return the index with the smallest average difference. If several indices tie, return the smallest of them.

nums = [2, 5, 3, 9, 5, 3]
i=0: |2 - 5| = 3   i=1: |3 - 5| = 2   i=2: |3 - 5| = 2
i=3: |4 - 4| = 0   i=4: |4 - 3| = 1   i=5: |4 - 0| = 4
answer = 3
hints: Each index needs the sum of its head and the sum of its tail. Recomputing both costs O(n) per index.
The head sum grows by nums[i] as i moves right, and the tail sum is the total minus the head sum.

Keep a running head sum, derive the tail sum from the total, divide with integer (floor) division by i + 1 and by n - i - 1 (use 0 when the tail is empty), and update the best only on a strictly smaller difference so ties keep the earliest index.
editorial: Compute the total once. Sweeping i from left to right, maintain head, the sum of nums[0..i]. Then tail = total - head, and both averages come from floor division. The tail average is 0 when i = n - 1. Keep the index with the smallest difference; replacing the best only when the new difference is strictly smaller yields the smallest index among ties.

This is a one-pass prefix-sum sweep: O(n) time and O(1) space. The sums stay below 10<sup>9</sup> (10,000 elements of at most 100,000), which fits in 32 bits, although the averages are all that matter for the comparison. Because every value is non-negative, floor division behaves the same in every language.
solution:
def minAvgDiffIndex(nums):
    n = len(nums)
    total = sum(nums)
    head = 0
    best, best_i = None, 0
    for i, x in enumerate(nums):
        head += x
        tail = total - head
        a = head // (i + 1)
        b = tail // (n - i - 1) if i < n - 1 else 0
        d = abs(a - b)
        if best is None or d < best:
            best, best_i = d, i
    return best_i
